title: Kissed Molten British Vine Tomatoes Shepherds Pie
description: A quick-fix British dish featuring vine tomatoes in a jammy, molten shepherds pie, cooked using the papillote method for a shojin-friendly meal. This recipe combines the flavors of fresh tomatoes with the comfort of a traditional shepherds pie.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat and saute the chopped onion until translucent.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture cook while preparing the papillote.
Cut a piece of parchment paper into a large square and place a vine tomato in the center.
Spoon the mushroom and tomato mixture over the tomato, leaving a 1 inch border around the tomato.
Fold the parchment paper over the filling, creating a tight seal.
Place the papillote on a baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes.
While the papillote is baking, prepare the mashed potatoes according to package instructions.
Remove the papillote from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes.
To assemble the shepherds pie, place the cooked papillote on the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish, then top with the mashed potatoes and shredded cheddar cheese.
Return the dish to the oven and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
